## Motivation DeepSeek V4.1 Flash was not yet supported under the EPD (Encode-Prefill-Decode) disaggregation pipeline. This PR extends the existing support to cover DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, enabling disaggregated serving where the vision encoder runs on a separate encode server and the language model runs on a prefill server.Then we went a step further and made optimizations on e-p pipeline and encode server effiency. Dsv4.1 vit rope kernel opt was separated as #44451. ## Modifications - support EPD pipeline on DeepSeek V4.1. - Allow DeepseekV4ForCausalLM in the EPD encoder model list and add --encoder-only ViT/aligner loading. - Add preprocess_mm_for_encoder / encoder token counting for the DSV4.1 sentinel image span. - Add prefill get_mm_data to splice encoder embeddings by img_grid_thw; skip decode image reprocess on MM pad sentinels. - ~~support Mooncake tp_broadcast opt.~~ - ~~Let only TP0 pull Mooncake RDMA embeddings; other ranks wait for broadcast.~~ - ~~Broadcast embedding buffer + MM metadata via tp_group.broadcast_tensor_dict.~~ - ~~Cut encoder→Prefill RDMA fanout from TP-wide to a single receiver rank.~~ - separate image loader. - Extract multiprocess image decoding into a dedicated image_loader module. - Feed preloaded images into preprocess so decode and HF/model preprocess stay aligned. - Overlap media I/O with the encoder event loop without changing preprocess semantics. - overlap the process_mm_item with vit encode. - Add a two-stage CPU preprocess → GPU forward pipeline when image loader is enabled. - Split dispatch into prep / forward workers so the next batch preprocesses while the current batch encodes. - Run ViT forward on a dedicated thread to keep the asyncio loop free during GPU work. - support optimized vit rope kernel .[#44451 ] - Add a fused CUDA kernel for vision apply_rotary / apply_vision_rotary. - Keep the same API as the eager path and gate it with SGLANG_DSV41_VIT_ROPE_CUDA. - ~~add dsv4.1 vit cuda graph and unify cuda graph envs.~~ - ~~Add Dsv41ViTCudaGraphRunner with shape-keyed capture / replay for ViT forward.~~ - ~~Unify Kimi-K3 and DSV4.1 under shared SGLANG_VIT_CUDA_GRAPH_* envs (with aliases).~~ ## Accuracy Tests In the DeepSeek V4.1 Flash tech report, the VLM benchmark dataset appears to have only been used to test the base model. The ViT RoPE kernel would be better as its own PR, since it isn't EPD-only. As for CUDA graph, TP broadcast and the send pool, I'd drop them from this PR for now and send each one separately once its benefit is validated.

For context, I ran a stepwise ablation of each feature on 8×H20-3e (DSV4.1 Flash, TP8 language-only prefill + encoder over Mooncake, single node):

- **Overlap (image loader + two-stage preprocess/forward pipeline):** a clear win when the encoder is the bottleneck, with ~33–38% lower mean TTFT and +13–23% throughput on an image-heavy workload. When prefill is the bottleneck, the encoder still gets faster (/encode −29%), but end-to-end TTFT barely moves.

issue_comments.body: @ZhengWG Could you please take a look at this PR?

Thanks for the work! Overall, I'd suggest keeping this PR focused on the main win, i.e. DSV4.1 EPD support plus the overlap pipeline. The ViT RoPE kernel would be better as its own PR, since it isn't EPD-only. As for CUDA graph, TP broadcast and the send pool, I'd drop them from this PR for now and send each one separately once its benefit is validated.

For context, I ran a stepwise ablation of each feature on 8×H20-3e (DSV4.1 Flash, TP8 language-only prefill + encoder over Mooncake, single node):

- **Overlap (image loader + two-stage preprocess/forward pipeline):** a clear win when the encoder is the bottleneck, with ~33–38% lower mean TTFT and +13–23% throughput on an image-heavy workload. When prefill is the bottleneck, the encoder still gets faster (/encode −29%), but end-to-end TTFT barely moves.
- **ViT RoPE kernel:** a small but consistent gain, ~2–6% TTFT (the kernel itself is ~5.5× faster than eager). It also changes the colocate DSV4.1 path, not just EPD.
- **ViT CUDA graph, Mooncake TP broadcast, encoder send pool:** no noticeable gain in my local tests, all within ±1% TTFT.
